claim: 25 riboswitch classes were previously known that selectively respond to ligands that are chemical derivatives of RNA monomers or their precursors.
source: Previously, 25 riboswitch classes were known that selectively respond to ligands that are chemical derivatives of RNA monomers or their precursors (McCown et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to McCown et al., 2017

claim: The strong bias in favor of RNA-like ligands strengthens the hypothesis that many widely-distributed riboswitch classes are direct descendants from the RNA World.
source: This strong bias in favor of RNA-like ligands strengthens the hypothesis (Nelson and Breaker, 2017; Breaker, 2010) that many of the widely-distributed riboswitch classes are direct descendants from the RNA World – a time before genetically-encoded protein biosynthesis (Gilbert, 1986; Benner et al., 1989).
evidence: Supported by citations to Nelson and Breaker, 2017; Breaker, 2010; Gilbert, 1986; Benner et al., 1989

claim: Guanidine-I riboswitches constituted approximately 70% of the original ykkC motif RNAs.
source: After removing guanidine-I riboswitches (subtype 1), which constituted ~70% of the original ykkC motif RNAs, we further separated the remaining collection of ykkC RNA variants (subtype 2).
evidence: Stated as a result of bioinformatic analysis

claim: ykkC subtype 2 RNAs were populated by multiple riboswitch classes that sensed distinct ligands.
source: Upon further investigation of the RNA sequences, the phylogeny of organisms containing these RNAs, and the genes associated with each instance of the RNA, we concluded that ykkC subtype 2 RNAs were populated by multiple riboswitch classes that sensed distinct ligands.
evidence: Based on bioinformatic analysis of sequences, phylogeny, and gene associations

claim: Subtype 2 representatives were sorted into four candidate riboswitch classes called subtypes 2a through 2d.
source: In total, these distinct representatives were sorted into four candidate riboswitch classes called subtypes 2a through 2d.
evidence: Result of bioinformatic sorting

claim: Nearly all highly-conserved nucleotides shared by ykkC RNAs are involved in forming tertiary contacts within the larger folded structure.
source: Nearly all highly-conserved nucleotides shared by ykkC RNAs are involved in forming tertiary contacts within the larger folded structure that positions other nucleotides to form the ligand-binding pocket.
evidence: Based on analysis of crystal structures of guanidine-I riboswitch

claim: Nucleotides that change identity and are characteristic of each subtype are almost exclusively found in close proximity to the known binding pocket of guanidine-I riboswitches.
source: However, nucleotides that change identity and are characteristic of each subtype are almost exclusively found in close proximity to the known binding pocket of guanidine-I riboswitches (indicated by black asterisks in Figure 1A).
evidence: Based on comparison with crystal structures and sequence analysis shown in Figure 1A

claim: ykkC subtype 2a RNAs were experimentally verified as a riboswitch class that responds to the bacterial alarmone ppGpp.
source: Shortly thereafter, these were experimentally verified as a riboswitch class that responds to the bacterial alarmone ppGpp (ME Sherlock, N Sudarsan, RR Breaker, manuscript submitted).
evidence: Supported by citation to manuscript submitted

claim: Representatives of ykkC subtype 2b riboswitch class commonly associate with genes for de novo purine biosynthesis.
source: First, representatives of this riboswitch class commonly associate with genes for de novo purine biosynthesis (Figure 1C).
evidence: Based on bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 1C

claim: Cytosine deaminase (codA), a gene involved in pyrimidine salvage, is known to be repressed by the purine guanine.
source: In addition, cytosine deaminase (codA), a gene involved in pyrimidine salvage that is known to be repressed by the purine guanine (Kilstrup et al., 1989), is also commonly located downstream of subtype 2b RNAs.
evidence: Supported by citation to Kilstrup et al., 1989

claim: There are 257 examples of ykkC subtype 2b RNAs distributed throughout bacteria of the phylum Firmicutes.
source: Second, there are 257 examples of ykkC subtype 2b RNAs distributed throughout bacteria of the phylum Firmicutes.
evidence: Result of bioinformatic search

claim: 127 examples of ykkC subtype 2b RNAs occur in a tandem arrangement with a guanine aptamer located directly upstream.
source: Of these, 127 examples occur in a tandem arrangement (Sudarsan et al., 2006) with a guanine aptamer (Mandal et al., 2003) located directly upstream (Figure 1B).
evidence: Result of bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 1B, with citations to Sudarsan et al., 2006 and Mandal et al., 2003

claim: Tandem riboswitch arrangements are likely to function in concert as two-input molecular logic gates.
source: Such tandem arrangements are likely to function in concert as two-input molecular logic gates (; Stoddard and Batey, 2006; Lee et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Stoddard and Batey, 2006 and Lee et al., 2010

claim: Guanine riboswitches typically turn off expression of downstream purine biosynthesis genes when sufficient guanine is present.
source: Guanine riboswitches typically turn off expression of downstream purine biosynthesis genes when sufficient guanine is present (Mandal et al., 2003), while representatives of ykkC subtype 2b riboswitches were predicted to turn on expression of downstream genes.
evidence: Supported by citation to Mandal et al., 2003

claim: Representatives of ykkC subtype 2b riboswitches were predicted to turn on expression of downstream genes.
source: Guanine riboswitches typically turn off expression of downstream purine biosynthesis genes when sufficient guanine is present (Mandal et al., 2003), while representatives of ykkC subtype 2b riboswitches were predicted to turn on expression of downstream genes.
evidence: Based on inference from tandem arrangement and gene associations

claim: The consensus sequence and structural models for ppGpp riboswitch aptamers (subtype 2a) and subtype 2b RNAs are remarkably alike.
source: Third, we noticed that the consensus sequence and structural models for ppGpp riboswitch aptamers (subtype 2a) and subtype 2b RNAs are remarkably alike, including many similarities at the ligand binding site, suggesting that their ligands might also share some chemical features.
evidence: Based on comparison of consensus models

claim: A long-range C-G base-pair present in guanidine-I riboswitches is absent in ppGpp riboswitches.
source: Particularly notable was the observation that a long-range C-G base-pair present in guanidine-I riboswitches (Reiss et al., 2017; Battaglia et al., 2017) is absent in ppGpp riboswitches, but appears to again be present in subtype 2b RNAs.
evidence: Based on structural analysis with citations to Reiss et al., 2017 and Battaglia et al., 2017

claim: The 106 nucleotide purC RNA construct from F. ignava exhibits structural modulation at highly conserved nucleotide positions upon the addition of PRPP.
source: The 106 purC RNA construct exhibits structural modulation at highly conserved nucleotide positions upon the addition of PRPP (Figure 2B).
evidence: Demonstrated by in-line probing data shown in Figure 2B

claim: No structural modulation of the 106 purC RNA is observed when guanidine, ppGpp, or guanine are added.
source: In contrast, no structural modulation of the RNA is observed when the known ligands for the other ykkC subtypes (guanidine and ppGpp) or for the guanine riboswitch (guanine) are added.
evidence: Demonstrated by in-line probing data in Figure 2B

claim: The structural changes selectively brought about by PRPP largely occur in regions equivalent to those previously implicated in ligand binding by guanidine-I and ppGpp riboswitch classes.
source: Importantly, the structural changes selectively brought about by PRPP largely occur in regions equivalent to those previously implicated in ligand binding by guanidine-I (Nelson et al., 2017; Reiss et al., 2017; Battaglia et al., 2017) and ppGpp riboswitch classes.
evidence: Based on comparison with known structures, supported by citations

claim: PRPP extensively degrades into multiple breakdown products over the course of binding experiments.
source: Due to the well-characterized instability of the PRPP molecule (Dennis et al., 2000; Meola et al., 2003), especially under alkaline conditions and high Mg2+, PRPP extensively degrades into multiple breakdown products over the course of our binding experiments.
evidence: Supported by citations to Dennis et al., 2000 and Meola et al., 2003

claim: Transcription of a singlet PRPP riboswitch derived from the purB gene of H. modesticaldum produces a greater yield of full-length RNA when PRPP is added to the reaction.
source: Transcription of a singlet PRPP riboswitch derived from the purB gene of Heliobacterium modesticaldum (Figure 3A) produces a greater yield of full-length RNA when PRPP is added to the reaction (Figure 3B).
evidence: Demonstrated by transcription termination assay data shown in Figure 3B

claim: The concentration of PRPP necessary to achieve half maximal termination (T50) for the H. modesticaldum purB construct is less than 100 µM.
source: The concentration of PRPP necessary to achieve half maximal termination (T50) is less than 100 µM (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Determined from transcription termination assay data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1

claim: An RNA construct (M1) with disruptive mutations within the highly-conserved aptamer sequence yields the same fraction of terminated and full-length transcripts regardless of PRPP concentration.
source: In contrast, an RNA construct (M1) with disruptive mutations within the highly-conserved aptamer sequence yields the same fraction of terminated and full-length transcripts regardless of PRPP concentration (Figure 3B).
evidence: Demonstrated by transcription termination assay data shown in Figure 3B

claim: T50 values should not be considered equivalent to KD values.
source: Importantly, T50 values should not be considered equivalent to KD values.
evidence: Based on established knowledge about riboswitch kinetics

claim: Riboswitches evaluated by transcription termination assays operate under kinetic limitations, whereas KD values established by in-line probing can reach thermodynamic equilibrium.
source: Riboswitches evaluated by transcription termination assays operate under kinetic limitations, whereas KD values established by in-line probing can reach thermodynamic equilibrium (Wickiser et al., 2005a; Wickiser et al., 2005b; Gilbert et al., 2006; Rieder et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to Wickiser et al., 2005a; Wickiser et al., 2005b; Gilbert et al., 2006; Rieder et al., 2007

claim: The KD for PRPP binding to the H. modesticaldum aptamer is likely to be far better than the T50 values measured, which range between 40 and 90 µM.
source: Thus, the KD for PRPP binding to the H. modesticaldum aptamer is likely to be far better than the T50 values we measured for the H. modesticaldum purB construct, which range between 40 and 90 µM (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Inferred from the difference between kinetic and thermodynamic measurements, with data from Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1

claim: Deletion of the purF gene causes PRPP to accumulate when cells are starved for purines.
source: Deletion of the purF gene, which encodes the enzyme that catalyzes the first committed step of de novo purine biosynthesis (Figure 1C), causes PRPP to accumulate when cells are starved for purines.
evidence: Based on known metabolic pathway shown in Figure 1C

claim: The lacZ gene is expressed in glucose minimal medium in the ΔpurF strain, but not in the parental B. subtilis strain with a functional purF gene.
source: Accordingly, the lacZ gene is expressed (blue) in glucose minimal medium in the ΔpurF strain, but not (clear) in the parental B. subtilis strain with a functional purF gene (Figure 3D).
evidence: Demonstrated by reporter gene assay data shown in Figure 3D

claim: The riboswitch appears to sample a much greater dynamic range for gene expression in vivo than is observed with in vitro transcription termination assays.
source: Notably, the cells range from completely clearto a robust blue under these two conditions, indicating that gene expression is fully suppressed when no ligand is present. Thus, the riboswitch appears to sample a much greater dynamic range for gene expression in vivo than is observed with in vitro transcription termination assays.
evidence: Based on comparison of in vivo reporter data (Figure 3D) with in vitro transcription data

claim: A riboswitch-reporter fusion carrying a mutation (M2) in the terminator stem expresses lacZ under both WT and ΔpurF conditions.
source: A riboswitch-reporter fusion carrying a mutation (M2) in the terminator stem expresses lacZ under both conditions.
evidence: Demonstrated by reporter gene assay data shown in Figure 3D

claim: PRPP accumulation in cells induces gene expression.
source: These results demonstrate that PRPP accumulation in cells induce gene expression, which parallels our findings in vitro that PRPP binding by ykkC subtype 2b RNAs promotes transcription elongation (Figure 3B and Figure 3C).
evidence: Demonstrated by in vivo reporter data (Figure 3D) and in vitro transcription data (Figure 3B and Figure 3C)

claim: Each aptamer in the tandem guanine-PRPP arrangement appears to independently fold to form its characteristic structure.
source: Each aptamer appears to independently fold to form its characteristic structure and each exhibits typical structural modulation (Figure 4B) upon addition of its cognate ligand as previously observed for singlet guanine (Mandal et al., 2003) or PRPP (Figure 2B) aptamers.
evidence: Demonstrated by in-line probing data shown in Figure 4B, with citation to Mandal et al., 2003

claim: There are typically only 5 to 7 nucleotides separating the P1 stems of the guanine and PRPP aptamers in tandem arrangements.
source: Specifically, there are typically only 5 to 7 nucleotides separating the P1 stems of the guanine and PRPP aptamers, suggesting this juxtaposition is important for logic gate function.
evidence: Based on bioinformatic analysis of tandem arrangements

claim: The addition of PRPP to the tandem construct causes a reduction in spontaneous RNA cleavage within the conserved nucleotides at the 5´ terminus of the PRPP aptamer.
source: Second, the addition of PRPP to the tandem construct causes a reduction in spontaneous RNA cleavage within the conserved nucleotides at the 5´ terminus of the PRPP aptamer (Figure 4B, region 5), whereas guanine addition causes this same region to experience a dramatic increase in scission.
evidence: Demonstrated by in-line probing data shown in Figure 4B

claim: Guanine addition causes the conserved nucleotides at the 5´ terminus of the PRPP aptamer to experience a dramatic increase in scission.
source: Second, the addition of PRPP to the tandem construct causes a reduction in spontaneous RNA cleavage within the conserved nucleotides at the 5´ terminus of the PRPP aptamer (Figure 4B, region 5), whereas guanine addition causes this same region to experience a dramatic increase in scission.
evidence: Demonstrated by in-line probing data shown in Figure 4B

claim: Guanine binding to its aptamer destabilizes an important structural feature necessary for ligand binding by the PRPP aptamer.
source: These results suggest that guanine binding to its aptamer destabilizes an important structural feature necessary for ligand binding by the PRPP aptamer.
evidence: Inferred from in-line probing data showing increased scission in PRPP aptamer region upon guanine addition

claim: The addition of PRPP increases the fraction of RNA transcripts that pass beyond the intrinsic terminator stem and reach full length in the tandem guanine-PRPP riboswitch.
source: Consistent with results from the singlet aptamer, the addition of PRPP increases the fraction of RNA transcripts that pass beyond the intrinsic terminator stem and reach full length (Figure 5B).
evidence: Demonstrated by transcription termination assay data shown in Figure 5B

claim: The addition of guanine causes an increase in the fraction of terminated transcripts in the tandem guanine-PRPP riboswitch.
source: Also as predicted, the addition of guanine causes an increase in the fraction of terminated transcripts.
evidence: Demonstrated by transcription termination assay data shown in Figure 5B

claim: When both guanine and PRPP are at high levels, the fraction of terminated products approaches zero in the tandem guanine-PRPP riboswitch.
source: When both guanine and PRPP are at high levels, the predicted genetic override occurs, and the fraction of terminated products approaches zero.
evidence: Demonstrated by transcription termination assay data shown in Figure 5B

claim: Mutations in M3 alter two highly-conserved nucleotides in the core of the guanine aptamer that are known to be essential for forming its ligand-binding core.
source: Specifically, the mutations in M3 alter two highly-conserved nucleotides in the core of the guanine aptamer that are known to be essential for forming its ligand-binding core (Batey et al., 2004; Serganov et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to Batey et al., 2004 and Serganov et al., 2004

claim: The addition of guanine does not increase transcription termination in the M3 mutant construct.
source: As expected, the addition of guanine does not increase transcription termination.
evidence: Demonstrated by transcription termination assay data shown in Figure 5B for M3 construct

claim: The mutations in M4 alter two highly-conserved nucleotides in PRPP aptamer, which are expected to disrupt PRPP binding.
source: Similarly, the mutations in M4 alter two highly-conserved nucleotides in PRPP aptamer, which we expect to disrupt PRPP binding.
evidence: Based on knowledge of conserved nucleotides and their role in ligand binding

claim: The M5 construct appears to be unaffected by the addition of either guanine or PRPP.
source: Indeed, the M5 construct appears to be unaffected by the addition of either guanine or PRPP (Figure 5B).
evidence: Demonstrated by transcription termination assay data shown in Figure 5B

claim: The relative concentrations of guanine and PRPP dictate the fraction of RNA transcripts that reach full length in the tandem riboswitch system.
source: The data from these reactions yields a 3D landscape demonstrating again that the relative concentrations of guanine and PRPP dictate the fraction of RNA transcripts that reach full length (Figure 5D).
evidence: Demonstrated by transcription termination assay data shown in Figure 5D

claim: The tandem riboswitch arrangement permits cells to tune the expression levels of associated genes based on the relative concentrations of guanine and PRPP.
source: Thus, the tandem riboswitch arrangement permits cells to tune the expression levels of associated genes based on the relative concentrations of guanine and PRPP, such that high PRPP levels promote purine production despite the abundance of guanine, a prominent purine.
evidence: Inferred from transcription termination assay data showing variable output based on ligand concentrations

claim: Each RNA molecule carrying the tandem guanine-PRPP aptamer arrangement functions as a Boolean IMPLY logic gate.
source: In this regard, each RNA molecule carrying this tandem aptamer arrangement functions as a Boolean IMPLY logic gate.
evidence: Inferred from the pattern of gene expression based on ligand presence/absence

claim: Gene expression should be on when neither ligand is present in the IMPLY logic gate formed by tandem guanine-PRPP aptamers.
source: The truth table for an IMPLY logic gate (Figure 6A) indicates that gene expression should be on when neither ligand is present, and when PRPP is bound by the RNA – even when guanine is available.
evidence: Based on the definition of IMPLY logic gate shown in Figure 6A

claim: Gene expression should be on when PRPP is bound by the RNA, even when guanine is available, in the IMPLY logic gate.
source: The truth table for an IMPLY logic gate (Figure 6A) indicates that gene expression should be on when neither ligand is present, and when PRPP is bound by the RNA – even when guanine is available.
evidence: Based on the definition of IMPLY logic gate shown in Figure 6A

claim: Gene expression should be off when guanine is bound by the RNA while PRPP is not, in the IMPLY logic gate.
source: Finally, gene expression should be off when guanine is bound by the RNA, which should occur when guanine is abundant while PRPP is not.
evidence: Based on the definition of IMPLY logic gate

claim: When transcription termination or gene expression is observed as the average output from a population of RNA constructs, the resulting data do not represent a perfect Boolean function because the output yields intermediate values.
source: When transcription termination or gene expression is observed as the average output from a population of RNA constructs, the resulting data do not represent a perfect Boolean function because the output yields intermediate values between zero and maximal values.
evidence: Based on analysis of population-level transcription data

claim: Each of the individual RNAs in the tandem riboswitch system operates as a binary logic gate that is either on or off.
source: Whereas each of the individual RNAs operates as a binary logic gate that is either on or off, a population of these RNAs exceeds the function of an individual Boolean logic gate.
evidence: Based on understanding of single-molecule behavior versus population behavior

claim: The output of the tandem riboswitch population functions more like a molecular rheostat to tune gene expression based on relative ligand concentrations.
source: Together, the output of the tandem riboswitch population functions more like a molecular rheostat to tune gene expression based on relative ligand concentrations, rather than as an all-or-nothing binary switch.
evidence: Inferred from the variable output observed at different ligand concentrations

claim: When ligand concentrations are at their extreme values, the output of the tandem system approaches the binary logic of an IMPLY gate.
source: Regardless, when ligand concentrations are at their extreme values, the output of the tandem system (Figure 5D) approaches the binary logic of an IMPLY gate.
evidence: Demonstrated by transcription termination assay data shown in Figure 5D

claim: During the stringent response in Firmicutes, nutrient starvation is signaled by the presence of uncharged tRNAs that activate the ppGpp synthase RelA.
source: During the stringent response in Firmicutes, nutrient starvation is signaled by the presence of uncharged tRNAs that activate the ppGpp synthase RelA (Geiger and Wolz, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Geiger and Wolz, 2014

claim: ppGpp synthesis causes GTP levels to drop and the transcriptional repressor CodY to release and enable transcription of branched-chain amino acid biosynthesis genes.
source: ppGpp synthesis causes GTP levels to drop and the transcriptional repressor CodY, which requires GTP and isoleucine to bind its target sites, to release and enable transcription of branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) biosynthesis genes (Sonenshein, 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sonenshein, 2005

claim: The resulting increased ppGpp concentration promotes binding of this signaling molecule as an inhibitor of enzymes such as GuaB, GMK, and HprT to suppress GTP production.
source: The resulting increased ppGpp concentration promotes binding of this signaling molecule as an inhibitor of enzymes such as GuaB, GMK, and HprT (Figure 1C) to suppress GTP production (Kriel et al., 2012), causing both guanine and PRPP to accumulate.
evidence: Supported by citation to Kriel et al., 2012 and shown in Figure 1C

claim: ppGpp inhibition of GuaB, GMK, and HprT causes both guanine and PRPP to accumulate.
source: The resulting increased ppGpp concentration promotes binding of this signaling molecule as an inhibitor of enzymes such as GuaB, GMK, and HprT (Figure 1C) to suppress GTP production (Kriel et al., 2012), causing both guanine and PRPP to accumulate.
evidence: Supported by citation to Kriel et al., 2012 and metabolic pathway shown in Figure 1C

claim: The genes associated with the tandem riboswitch system only include those for catalyzing the steps of de novo purine synthesis up to the production of inosine monophosphate (IMP).
source: At first this appears counterintuitive, but the genes associated with the tandem riboswitch system only include those for catalyzing the steps of de novo purine synthesis up to the production of inosine monophosphate (IMP), the branch point between AMP and GMP production (Figure 1C).
evidence: Based on bioinformatic analysis of gene associations shown in Figure 1C

claim: The riboswitch promotes AMP synthesis, but will not turn on genes specific for GDP or GTP synthesis that are already being inhibited by ppGpp.
source: Thus, the riboswitch promotes AMP synthesis, but will not turn on genes specific for GDP or GTP synthesis that are already being inhibited by ppGpp.
evidence: Inferred from gene associations and metabolic pathway

claim: ATP is known to be present in elevated quantities during the stringent response because it is used as the initiating nucleotide for transcription of genes under the ppGpp superregulon.
source: ATP is known to be present in elevated quantities during the stringent response because it is used as the initiating nucleotide for transcription of genes under the ppGpp superregulon, whereas rRNA transcripts utilize GTP as the initiating nucleotide to suppress protein production (Krásný et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Krásný et al., 2008

claim: The guanine-PRPP tandem riboswitch arrangement at its functional limits most closely approximates an IMPLY logic gate.
source: As noted above, the guanine-PRPP tandem riboswitch arrangement at its functional limits most closely approximates an IMPLY logic gate (Figure 6A).
evidence: Based on transcription termination assay data and logic gate analysis shown in Figure 6A

claim: Tandem S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) and adenosylcobalamin (AdoCbl) riboswitches form a NOR gate.
source: This all-RNA system joins the NOR gate formed by tandem S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) and adenosylcobalamin (AdoCbl or coenzyme B12) riboswitches (Sudarsan et al., 2006) (Figure 6B) and the AND gate formed by tandem T box and ppGpp riboswitch RNAs (Figure 6C) as sophisticated regulatory RNAs that approximate Boolean logic functions.
evidence: Supported by citation to Sudarsan et al., 2006 and shown in Figure 6B

claim: Tandem T box and ppGpp riboswitch RNAs form an AND gate.
source: This all-RNA system joins the NOR gate formed by tandem S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) and adenosylcobalamin (AdoCbl or coenzyme B12) riboswitches (Sudarsan et al., 2006) (Figure 6B) and the AND gate formed by tandem T box and ppGpp riboswitch RNAs (Figure 6C) as sophisticated regulatory RNAs that approximate Boolean logic functions.
evidence: Shown in Figure 6C

claim: The tandem riboswitch-ribozyme arrangement formed by a c-di-GMP-II riboswitch and a group I self-splicing ribozyme senses both c-di-GMP and guanosine to approximate the function of a Boolean AND gate.
source: Similarly, the tandem riboswitch-ribozyme arrangement formed by a c-di-GMP-II riboswitch and a group I self-splicing ribozyme senses both c-di-GMP and guanosine (or any of its 5´-phosphorylated derivatives) to approximate the function of a Boolean AND gate (Lee et al., 2010; Chen et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lee et al., 2010 and Chen et al., 2011

claim: PRPP is an essential precursor for the modern biosynthesis of RNA monomers in organisms from all three domains of life.
source: PRPP is an essential precursor for the modern biosynthesis of RNA monomers in organisms from all three domains of life, and is likely to have been important for the production of ribonucleotides very early in evolution.
evidence: Based on established biochemical knowledge

claim: PRPP is likely to have been important for the production of ribonucleotides very early in evolution.
source: PRPP is an essential precursor for the modern biosynthesis of RNA monomers in organisms from all three domains of life, and is likely to have been important for the production of ribonucleotides very early in evolution.
evidence: Inferred from its essential role in modern organisms

claim: Representatives of PRPP riboswitches were on the list of riboswitch candidates over a decade ago.
source: Intriguingly, we had representatives of PRPP riboswitches on our list of riboswitch candidates over a decade ago (Barrick et al., 2004), but due to their striking similarity to riboswitches for guanidine (Nelson et al., 2017) and ppGpp, they were unusually difficult to identify and experimentally validate.
evidence: Supported by citation to Barrick et al., 2004

claim: PRPP riboswitches were unusually difficult to identify and experimentally validate due to their striking similarity to riboswitches for guanidine and ppGpp.
source: Intriguingly, we had representatives of PRPP riboswitches on our list of riboswitch candidates over a decade ago (Barrick et al., 2004), but due to their striking similarity to riboswitches for guanidine (Nelson et al., 2017) and ppGpp, they were unusually difficult to identify and experimentally validate.
evidence: Based on the authors' experience with bioinformatic and experimental analysis

claim: Guanine riboswitches have undergone one or a few key mutations to change their ligand specificity to adenine.
source: For example, guanine riboswitches have undergone one or a few key mutations to change their ligand specificity to adenine (Mandal and Breaker, 2004) or 2´-deoxyguanosine (Kim et al., 2007; Weinberg et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Mandal and Breaker, 2004; Kim et al., 2007; Weinberg et al., 2017

claim: Guanine riboswitches have undergone one or a few key mutations to change their ligand specificity to 2´-deoxyguanosine.
source: For example, guanine riboswitches have undergone one or a few key mutations to change their ligand specificity to adenine (Mandal and Breaker, 2004) or 2´-deoxyguanosine (Kim et al., 2007; Weinberg et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kim et al., 2007 and Weinberg et al., 2017

claim: Subtle binding site variants of FMN riboswitches appear to bind a closely related ligand.
source: Also, subtle binding site variants of FMN riboswitches appear to bind a closely related ligand (https://patentscope.wipo.int/search/en/detail.jsf?docId=WO2011097027&recNum=27&docAn=US2011000204&queryString=(riboswitch)%2520&maxRec=179; Weinberg et al., 2017), and riboswitches for molybdenum cofactor (MoCo) are proposed to have modest binding site changes to alter their ligand specificity to bind tungsten cofactor (Regulski et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by patent citation and citation to Weinberg et al., 2017

claim: Riboswitches for molybdenum cofactor (MoCo) are proposed to have modest binding site changes to alter their ligand specificity to bind tungsten cofactor.
source: Also, subtle binding site variants of FMN riboswitches appear to bind a closely related ligand (https://patentscope.wipo.int/search/en/detail.jsf?docId=WO2011097027&recNum=27&docAn=US2011000204&queryString=(riboswitch)%2520&maxRec=179; Weinberg et al., 2017), and riboswitches for molybdenum cofactor (MoCo) are proposed to have modest binding site changes to alter their ligand specificity to bind tungsten cofactor (Regulski et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Regulski et al., 2008

claim: The ppGpp and PRPP riboswitch ligands differ by the presence or absence of a guanine nucleobase and by the location and number of phosphate moieties.
source: The ppGpp (subtype 2a) and PRPP (subtype 2b) riboswitch ligands differ by the presence or absence of a guanine nucleobase and by the location and number of phosphate moieties.
evidence: Based on chemical structures of the ligands

claim: Guanidinium forms only a portion of the purine ring of ppGpp.
source: Guanidinium, the ligand for guanidine-I (subtype 1) riboswitches is entirely distinct from PRPP, and this moiety forms only a portion of the purine ring of ppGpp.
evidence: Based on chemical structures

claim: The ligands sensed by ykkC subtypes 2c and 2d still remain to be discovered.
source: The ligands sensed by subtypes 2 c and 2d, which are associated with genes encoding nucleoside diphosphate linked to X (NUDIX) hydrolases of unknown specificity and a transporter of unknown function associated with phosphonate utilization (phn_DUF6), respectively, still remain to be discovered.
evidence: Stated as current state of knowledge

claim: ykkC subtype 2c RNAs are associated with genes encoding nucleoside diphosphate linked to X (NUDIX) hydrolases of unknown specificity.
source: The ligands sensed by subtypes 2 c and 2d, which are associated with genes encoding nucleoside diphosphate linked to X (NUDIX) hydrolases of unknown specificity and a transporter of unknown function associated with phosphonate utilization (phn_DUF6), respectively, still remain to be discovered.
evidence: Based on bioinformatic analysis of gene associations

claim: ykkC subtype 2d RNAs are associated with a transporter of unknown function associated with phosphonate utilization (phn_DUF6).
source: The ligands sensed by subtypes 2 c and 2d, which are associated with genes encoding nucleoside diphosphate linked to X (NUDIX) hydrolases of unknown specificity and a transporter of unknown function associated with phosphonate utilization (phn_DUF6), respectively, still remain to be discovered.
evidence: Based on bioinformatic analysis of gene associations

claim: The consensus model for subtype 2c RNAs has the most similarity to those for PRPP and ppGpp riboswitches.
source: Because the consensus model for subtype 2c RNAs has the most similarity to those for PRPP and ppGpp riboswitches, and the associated genes encode enzymes with various nucleotide substrates, we speculate that this candidate riboswitch class senses another nucleotide derivative.
evidence: Based on comparison of consensus models

claim: Subtype 2c candidate riboswitch class is speculated to sense another nucleotide derivative.
